subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 19-year-old man presents with 3 weeks of painless, progressive vision loss in the right eye, followed 2 months later by similar loss in the left eye. Funduscopy shows optic disc hyperemia, and visual acuity is 20/200 bilaterally. His maternal uncle and a maternal cousin had similar vision loss, whereas his father and paternal relatives are unaffected. Genetic testing reveals a mitochondrial DNA mutation affecting a complex I subunit.
question: Which of the following best explains the inheritance pattern of this disorder?

options.text: Autosomal dominant inheritance with incomplete penetrance

explanation_correct: Leber hereditary optic neuropathy is caused by mitochondrial DNA mutations, which are transmitted only through the mother; all offspring of an affected female may inherit the mutation. Variable expression results from heteroplasmy, the coexistence of mutant and normal mitochondrial genomes within cells.

explanation_incorrect.A: Autosomal dominant inheritance would require an affected parent of either sex to transmit the allele with a 50% risk, which does not match the purely maternal pattern.
explanation_incorrect.B: Autosomal recessive inheritance would not show the maternal transmission pattern described.
explanation_incorrect.C: X-linked recessive inheritance affects males predominantly but is transmitted by carrier mothers and would not explain the purely maternal pattern seen in his relatives.
explanation_incorrect.E: Genomic imprinting involves parent-of-origin-specific expression of nuclear genes and is not the mechanism of mitochondrial DNA disorders.

educationalObjective: Mitochondrial DNA disorders such as Leber hereditary optic neuropathy are transmitted maternally, with variable expression due to heteroplasmy.
